(1) The reactivity of doped ceria with methane was not significantly different than that of undoped ceria, (2) Nb-doped cerium oxide was able to oxidize carbon deposits at lower temperature than undoped or gadolinia doped ceria, and (3) The presence of oxygen vacancies was found to be important in the ability of ceria to oxidize carbon.
doping with Nb is beneficial in reducing the carbon deposition rate, and in promoting carbon oxidation.

the addition of Gd or Nb to ceria does not significantly alter the reactivity of ceria towards methane, but Nb does enhance the ability of ceria to oxidise carbon at lower temperatures than Gd-doped or undoped ceria.

the influence of point defects in ceria on its resistance to carbon deposition in methane catalytic oxidation, and the ability to oxidize carbon deposits.

the presence of point defects in ceria does not appear to have an influence on the resistance of the material to carbon deposition in methane catalysis.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the addition of Gd to ceria does not affect the resistance of the ceria to carbon formation and oxidation, but the addition of 5% Nb to ceria improves its resistance to carbon formation and carbon oxidation.

the presence of point defects on a ceria surface is a necessary condition for carbon oxidation, but that the presence of these defects alone is not sufficient to promote carbon oxidation at low temperatures.

doping ceria with either Nb or Gd has a minor influence on the catalytic properties of ceria for methane oxidation and that doping with Gd has little influence on the ability of ceria to oxidize deposited carbon at 900°C.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cerium is a relatively resistant metal for the catalytic oxidation of methane, and that the resistance of cerium to carbon deposition can be improved by doping.

the addition of point defects, either by doping or by the creation of vacancies during reduction, does not significantly alter the resistance of cerium oxide to carbon deposition in methane conversion reactions.
ceria can be used as a catalyst in methane conversion without carbon deposition, but the addition of dopants such as Nb can increase the resistance to carbon deposition.
